- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect market resilience or reversal.
- Model frequently overreacts to recent spikes (e.g., +5–10% in 1–2 days), leading to over-forecasted peaks; apply lagged smoothing or dampen momentum.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., price drops after spike), model often fails to recognize it; add a 1–2 day lagged correction or use recent 7-day average as baseline.
- When sentiment shifts from positive to negative (or vice versa), model often misjudges direction; align forecast with sentiment transition, not just latest value.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate later days (especially 20–30) when sentiment is bullish; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent 14-day high to avoid overextension.
